newsitem.title: GERMANY: BSE, grain refunds pressure EU farm budget-Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: BSE, grain refunds pressure EU farm budget-Toepfer.

text.p: The 1996/97 European Union farm budget would come under pressure from planned measures to boost the beef market and by the need to subsidise grain exports, German grain trader Toepfer said in its monthly market report.
Falling world grain prices saw the EU return to wheat and barley refunds when soaring global prices in 95/96 helped it save money and even collect wheat and barley export taxes.
But prices moved sharply lower in the 96/97 season.
Toepfer said the levels of roughly 16 Ecus a tonne for wheat export rebates and 31 Ecus for barley seen over the last two weeks looked set to become the "bottom range for the next few months."
This would take additional funds out of the farm budget.
The 1995/96 budget, ended Oct 15, 1996, brought a 1.7 billion Ecu surplus.
A repeat was not only unlikely because of the grain costs but also because the EU approved extra aid to help farmers through the crisis caused by so-called mad cow disease.
Farm ministers in October approved spending of 1.83 billion Ecus on additional beef market support measures and direct aid to beef farmers, Toepfer noted.
Farm spending in 1996 accounted for 49.5 percent of the total budget.
